impl.summary: Audio → Edit speech with Tencent AuK, on the open engine only. Edit a line of the transcript and only the smallest changed span of words is re-spoken. Each change gets its own window, cut at silences, with at least 1 s of untouched speech on each side and kept inside AuK's 30 s budget (source plus output). The window is crossfaded back with no clicks. Pitch, pace, volume, emotion, whisper and normal voice, Clean up, and Keep only this speaker work on ticked lines the same way. On a video, the new sound goes back on with the picture stream-copied, and the page warns and offers Lipsync. Also added: Fix this line in the Captions editor, an Edit speech item in the ⋯ menu of audio and video results, the Assist/MCP tool edit_speech, a row on the GPU pre-flight board, the ComfyUI-AuK pack pinned with an MIT licence row, and a second graph, speech-tts-auk, for AuK text to speech. Nothing from this plan existed in the base; everything was built new. Pushed at a66b9538. Commits are signed.

impl.docsNotes: STATUS/ARCHITECTURE not edited. For the docs pass: (1) Audio → Edit speech (/audio/edit-speech), open engine only. AuK is MIT, but it needs the Qwen2.5-Omni-3B encoder, which is under the Qwen Research License (NON-COMMERCIAL), so the model reads as non-commercial in Models & licences. (2) Brief corrections from primary sources: the AuK README publishes VRAM (A800, bf16: ~25 GiB peak, ~17 GiB with the loader's cpu_offload), and the brief's 'automatic offload not supported' needs that nuance (cpu_offload is opt-in); the 30 s limit is source + output per call, so a same-length effect takes at most ~14.7 s of source; AuK outputs 24 kHz mono; Qwen2.5-Omni-3B is 11.97 GB; languages are English and Chinese (arXiv 2609.08936: a bilingual corpus); the comfyui folder imports the auk package, so the whole repo must be installed with pip install -e .[comfyui]. Pinned commit 0d40366b (2026-10-27). (3) The brief's line numbers did not apply; the code was found by name. (4) The base had no voice-consent gate (voice design/clone carry only a 'Get consent for cloned voices' note), so Edit speech shows a plain consent line rather than a gate. (5) The Prompt Enhancer is always off: Fuobe writes the instruction and generation_seconds, and the UI says no language model sees the words.

findings.title: On a video, any edit that changes length puts all later speech out of sync with the picture
findings.where: src/lib/speech-edit.ts planTextWindows (seconds = old length + delta), planEffectWindows (pace), planSpeechEdit (video branch: oss-mux video-mux-audio-replace)
findings.detail: The edited soundtrack is muxed onto the stream-copied picture as it is. planSpeechEdit returns length 11.913 s for a 9 s clip after 'on Tuesday morning.' becomes 'on a very sunny Wednesday morning in late October.', and 4.6 s for Pace 2x over the whole 9 s clip (checked with a probe test). Every word after the edit then drifts by the difference, and with pace the second half of the clip is silent. The only video warning is that lips won't match the changed words, and the UI never shows the new length. Fix: for kind 'video', keep each window's generation_seconds equal to its old length (AuK re-times the words to fit it), or refuse or clearly warn about length-changing edits and Pace on a video.
findings.verified: probe test calling planSpeechEdit (removed afterwards); read video-mux-audio-replace.json (LoadVideo + LoadAudio + ConcatenateVideo + SaveVideo, nothing re-times the audio)

findings.title: Seams can click on loud recordings: ComfyUI's AudioMerge rescales any result that peaks above 1.0
findings.where: src/lib/av/speech-edit-graph.ts expandSpeechEditWorkflow (seam = a + (b - a) x fade-in, built from AudioMerge subtract, multiply and add)
findings.detail: Core AudioMerge (comfy_extras/nodes_audio.py, the execute method) ends with `if max_val > 1.0: waveform = waveform / max_val`. The seam's diff b - a is the original against AuK's version of the same moment, and the two are not phase-aligned, so it easily goes past 1.0 on speech mastered near 0 dBFS. Example: a = 0.8 and b = -0.5 give a diff of -1.3. The whole diff piece is then divided by its peak, so the seam ends at a + (b - a)/k instead of b, and the next piece (the edit's middle) starts at b: a step, heard as a click. The final add can also be normalised on its own. The implementer's no-click check used a quiet sine with a +6 dB stand-in for AuK, which doesn't reach this. Fix: scale both sides down before the seam math and back up after (e.g. AudioAdjustVolume -12 dB, then +12 dB), or crossfade without the diff (a x fade-out + b x fade-in with both curves written), and add a loud-signal case to the CPU check.

findings.title: Merging two nearby changes puts the old words' punctuation into AuK's new text
findings.where: src/lib/speech-edit.ts mergeChanges (`between` uses the old words with their punctuation)
findings.detail: 'on Tuesday morning.' → 'on a very sunny Wednesday morning in late October.' produces the instruction "Replace 'Tuesday morning.' with 'a very sunny Wednesday morning. in late October.'". The stray full stop in the middle asks AuK for a sentence break there. Fix: take the words between the two changes from the edited text, or strip the old words' trailing punctuation when merging.

Each window goes to AuK brought back to its own level (w{n}_in +12), AuK's output goes down again (w{n}_low -12), and the whole result comes up once before the save (out +12), so the net gain is 0 dB. fix.finalSummary: Edit speech (Audio → Edit speech, the ⋯ menu, Captions' Fix this line, Assist/MCP edit_speech) runs on the open engine only, with Tencent AuK on the person's ComfyUI. On the cloud engine it says it runs on your GPU (open source), and Paid APIs only hides or refuses it, since AuK is hosted on neither fal nor Replicate. After this fix, a video's edited sound keeps the clip's length, so it stays in step with the stream-copied picture. Pace is for audio only. Seams no longer click on loud recordings, verified on CPU ComfyUI with the core stitch nodes and a stand-in for AuK. What is verified: planning, diff and windows, graph expansion and stitch accuracy on CPU, provider bindings, routes, and the page in the browser in demo mode. What is built but not verified: AuK itself. It needs an NVIDIA GPU (about 17 to 25 GiB VRAM), the ComfyUI-AuK pack (AUK=1 in install-comfyui.sh) and about 19 GB of weights. No API key is involved. Public sign-up: guests see the page read-only. Accounts get a price check of their own file, priced for their own GPU and never a demo; the run answers own-gpu-tool at the proxy, like main's other audio tools.
